newsitem.title: CONGO: Brazzaville shelling, signs of mediation progress.
newsitem.headline: Brazzaville shelling, signs of mediation progress.

text.p: Renewed shelling rocked the battered Congo Republic capital Brazzaville on Saturday but there were signs of progress in mediation.

A spokesman for Bernard Kolelas, city mayor and president of a national mediation committee, said the shelling had delayed a planned statement on prospects for ending the political and ethnic clashes which have killed hundreds of people.
"Kolelas seems to be making progress with his negotiations," one diplomat told Reuters in Kinshasa.

The conflict between President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso began on June 5 when government troops surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militia ahead of planned July 27 elections.
Lissouba, Sassou and Kolelas had all been due to stand.
Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, is heading an international mediation effort.
Truces have come and gone. The fighting has put tens of thousands of civilians to flight and devastated whole districts of the normally sleepy capital.
One witness said Saturday's fighting was less intense than previously.
Kolelas supporters were at the centre of similar ethnic and political clashes that killed at least 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election.
